title: Design Content Moderation at Scale
summary: A moderation system for 50 million posts a day. The hard part is not the model, it is arithmetic: rare violations, base rates, tiered models that keep cost down, and human reviewers and appeals that keep errors honest.
objectives: Convert daily post volume into QPS, tokens, and the cost of classifying everything with a large versus a small model
Use Bayes' rule to compute precision at a given base rate, and explain why a good classifier still floods reviewers
Design a tiered cascade and compute its expected cost per item from pass-through fractions
Map score bands to actions (allow, demote, review, remove) and use appeals to estimate false-removal rates
Plan evaluation with labeler agreement, stratified audits and drift monitoring, and defend the trade-offs
prerequisites: Work through [A Framework for LLM System Design](/learn/llm-system-design/design-framework) first. It helps to know [guardrails and safe deployment](/learn/production-systems/guardrails) and [routing and cascades](/learn/production-systems/model-routing).
